title: Change of rings for sheaves of modules is left adjoint to restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, let $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $X$, let $\mathcal M$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules, and let $\mathcal N$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ for $\mathcal N$ as an $\mathcal A$-module through $a$, and $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ for the sheafified sectionwise tensor product with its $\mathcal B$-module structure [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The correspondence sending a $\mathcal B$-linear map $u:\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ to $m\mapsto u(1\otimes m)$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$, natural in both modules.

source.place: Tag 008A, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (line 1916), including its proof by the presheaf tensor adjunction and sheafification

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ be the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal A(U)}\mathcal M(U)$ with restrictions $b\otimes m\mapsto b|_V\otimes m|_V$ and $\mathcal B(U)$ acting on the left factor, a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; $\mathcal N$ and $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ are in particular presheaves of $\mathcal B$- and $\mathcal A$-modules. By the presheaf change-of-rings adjunction [lem-pc-presheaf-change-of-rings-adjunction] (Stacks 006R), $v\mapsto(m\mapsto v_U(1\otimes m))_U$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$ between morphisms of presheaves of modules, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$. Since $\mathcal M$ and $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ are sheaves, the right side is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$ in sheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules (morphisms of sheaves of modules are the morphisms of the underlying presheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]).

source.place: Tag 008A proof: 'This follows from Lemma 006R (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict-presheaves)', line 1933

proof.text: By definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$: its underlying sheaf of abelian groups is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups, and its $\mathcal B$-module structure is the unique one extending that of $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$; that is, it is the sheafification $\eta:\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M\to\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ of this presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] ($\mathcal B$ is a sheaf, so $\mathcal B^\#=\mathcal B$). By the universal property of that sheafification, since $\mathcal N$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules, $u\mapsto u\circ\eta$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)$, natural in $\mathcal N$ (post-composition) and in $\mathcal M$ (because $\eta$ is natural: for $f:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ the map $\mathrm{id}\otimes f$ of sheaves is by definition the unique map with $(\mathrm{id}\otimes f)\circ\eta_{\mathcal M}=\eta_{\mathcal M'}\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes_p f)$).

source.place: Tag 008A proof: 'Hom(O_2 (x)_{O_1} G, F) = Hom(O_2 (x)_{p,O_1} G, F) because F is a sheaf', lines 1934-1939, by Lemma 0089 (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and the adjunction formula after it (lines 1862-1872)

proof.text: Composing the bijections of steps 2 and 1 gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$, natural in both modules as a composite of natural bijections. It sends $u$ to $(m\mapsto(u\circ\eta)_U(1\otimes m))_U=(m\mapsto u(1\otimes m))_U$, where $1\otimes m$ in $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ denotes $\eta_U(1\otimes m)$; this is the correspondence of the statement.
